d.g: The absolute leader of a yakuza clan. He has an advisor called a saiko-komon.

oyabun.e: Borrowed from Japanese 親分 (literally “foster parent”).

d.g: Any of certain marine bivalve mollusks, especially those of the family Ostreidae (the true oysters), usually found adhering to rocks or other fixed objects in shallow water along the seacoasts, or in brackish water in the mouth of rivers.
d.x: Piſt. Why then the world's mine Oyſter, which I, with ſword will open.

d.g: The delicate oyster-shaped morsel of dark meat contained in a small cavity of the bone on each side of the lower part of the back of a fowl.
d.x: Cut remaining skin on back. Remove the oyster (choice dark meat in spoon-shaped bone on back) with the leg.

d.g: A pale beige color tinted with grey or pink, like that of an oyster.

d.x: Hard and sharp as flint, from which no steel had ever struck out generous fire; secret, and self-contained, and solitary as an oyster.

oyster.e: From Middle English oystre, from Old English ostre, reinforced or superseded by Anglo-Norman oistre, which is from Old French oistre, uistre (compare modern French huître); both lines (Old English and Old French) from Latin ostrea, from Ancient Greek ὄστρεον (óstreon). Doublet of ostro (“a purple dye”).

d.g: Any of several black or pied coastal wading birds in the genus Haematopus that have a long red or orange bill and feed on shellfish.
